record.original_question: For every positive integer n, the nth Mersenne number is M_n = 2^n - 1. Are there infinitely many composite Mersenne numbers?

evidence.quote: For every positive integer n, the nth Mersenne number is defined by M_n=2^n-1.
Hence, there remain several open problems about Mersenne primes: Are there infinitely many composite Mersenne numbers?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For each positive integer $n$, define the $n$-th Mersenne number by
$$M_n = 2^n - 1.$$
A Mersenne prime is a Mersenne number that is prime; otherwise $M_n$ is called a composite Mersenne number. It is well known that if $n$ is composite then $M_n$ is composite, so the interesting case is when the index is prime. 

Prove or disprove: there exist infinitely many prime numbers $p$ such that the Mersenne number $M_p = 2^p - 1$ is composite.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is classically listed as open: it is not known unconditionally whether infinitely many Mersenne numbers with prime index are composite, although it follows from various standard conjectures (e.g., infinitude of Sophie Germain primes $p \equiv 3 \pmod 4$).

status_evidence.title: Mersenne prime - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: It is not known whether the set of Mersenne primes is finite or infinite, nor whether infinitely many Mersenne numbers with prime exponent are composite.
status_evidence.claim: The infinitude of composite Mersenne numbers with prime index is an open question.
